sentence: A 48-year-old male patient, with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, systemic arterial hypertension and hypothyroidism, diagnosed 8 years ago, with inadequate control, as well as chronic renal failure of 2 years' duration, treated with hemodialysis.

He came with a two-week history of pain in the glans and irritative urinary symptoms; A week later he reported hypochromia in the glans, as well as a sensation of local anesthesia, and a violaceous lesion was added on the dorsal surface of the glans, which extended and was accompanied by a purulent secretion, for which he came to our service.
The physical examination revealed: the presence of a hypochromic, hypothermic glans with an area of ​​necrosis on the dorsum, accompanied by mild purulent and foul-smelling discharge.

The blood count reported: hemoglobin 8.02 g/dl, leukocytes 8,060, platelets 355,000; blood chemistry: glucose 277 mg/dl, creatinine 5.5 mg/dl, BUN 90.1 mg/dl; liver function tests: TGO 48, TGP 32, alkaline phosphatase 332, DHL 232; Serum electrolytes: sodium 128.8 mmol/l, potassium 6.28 mmol/l, chloride 96.4 mmol/l, calcium 7.92 mmol/l and phosphorus 7.36 mmol/l.
He underwent a partial phallectomy, without complications.
The pathological analysis reported: necrosis and acute and chronic inflammatory process, with abscess and ulceration, with arteriosclerosis obliterans.
The patient is currently under surveillance.
